Note::TexAccessor::warnings¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::warnings() const

Extract Compiler Diagnostics Embedded In Source Or Logs¶

warnings() extracts every occurrence of four recognized LaTeX diagnostic patterns, each as one whole-match token, in source order:

Pattern

Example match

\PackageWarning{pkg}{msg}

\PackageWarning{mypkg}{deprecated macro}

\PackageError{pkg}{msg}{help}

\PackageError{mypkg}{bad option}{See the docs.}

the literal text Undefined control sequence

Undefined control sequence

LaTeX Error: through the rest of the line

LaTeX Error: File not found

Unlike the semantic extractors that capture only a command’s brace body (such as captions or todos), warnings() captures the entire matched span, brace groups and all — the token for a \PackageWarning match is the whole command call, not just its message argument. This method is intended to run over compiler log text or source comments containing embedded diagnostics, not authored document prose, though it scans whatever Text it is given either way.

The LaTeX Error: pattern stops at the end of the physical line: text on a following line, even immediately after, is never included in that token. The other three patterns have no line boundary of their own — a \PackageWarning{...}{...} or \PackageError{...}{...}{...} call may itself span multiple lines if its brace arguments do.

The closed TokenBatch stores every extracted diagnostic in its rank-1 Text tokens() Note. Its Int64 offsets() has source.numel() + 1 entries, so flattened source cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). The receiver is not mutated.

Undefined yields undefined tokens with offsets [0]. Empty cells and cells with no recognized diagnostic produce empty intervals. Only Text is accepted.

Example 1: All Four Patterns, Including The Line Boundary¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\PackageWarning{mypkg}{deprecated macro} body)",
    R"(Undefined control sequence at line 12)",
    R"(LaTeX Error: File not found)"
    "\ntrailing text on the next line is not part of the match",
    "clean, no diagnostics here"});
const auto warnings = source.tex().warnings();

std::cout << warnings.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\PackageWarning{mypkg}{deprecated macro}", "Undefined control sequence", "LaTeX Error: File not found"]

The third cell’s LaTeX Error: token stops exactly at the newline; the “trailing text on the next line” is not part of the match, even though it immediately follows in the same cell. The fourth, clean cell contributes nothing.

Example 2: Per-Cell Offsets¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = warnings.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 1, 2, 3, 3]

Each of the first three cells owns exactly one diagnostic; the fourth owns none.

Example 3: A \PackageError Call, Whole-Match Captured¶

const auto error_batch =
    pluss::make_note({R"(\PackageError{mypkg}{bad option}{See the docs.})"})
        .tex().warnings();
std::cout << error_batch.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\\PackageError{mypkg}{bad option}{See the docs.}"]

All three brace groups — package name, message, and help text — are part of the single captured token.

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().warnings().tokens().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().warnings();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "warnings Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
warnings Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • todos: extract authoring notes instead of compiler diagnostics.

  • strip_comments: remove %-comments before scanning, if comment text should not be mistaken for a diagnostic.
